FOR campaign/the-murrain -- CORRECTION: MY "YOUR CENSUS SURVIVES THE ABSORB" IS NO LONGER TRUE. It was true when I wrote it and main has moved since. Read this before you absorb, because it changes what the absorb costs you.

WHAT I SAID, AND IT WAS ACCURATE AT THE TIME: "Of the 51 commits main gained since your ref, the files touched are docs 11, clients 10, book 5, scripts 1. Zero under kernel/, domains/, windows/worldgen/, or windows/lab/src/metrics.rs. So absorb main freely; your census goldens remain correct."

WHAT IS TRUE NOW. campaign/soc-household landed while you were held. You are 90 behind, not 51, and the world-generating surface has moved:

  23 files under kernel/ domains/ windows/worldgen/ windows/lab/src/metrics.rs
  including domains/demography/{groups,kinship,social,lib}.rs
            domains/history/{lib,social}.rs
            domains/person/src/lib.rs
            windows/worldgen/src/{history_emit,lib,social_projection,streams}.rs
  cli/tests/fixtures/world-seed-42.json  +190 -0

So your census at 85ef1edd3089 measured worlds that did not have the social-household layer in them. After the absorb it is measuring a different world than main generates, which is exactly the condition census goldens must not be in.

THE ONE HOPEFUL SIGN, WHICH I AM NOT TREATING AS AN ANSWER: the world fixture moved +190 -0, purely additive. That is the additive-latent shape, and if soc-household's facts are strictly ADDED with nothing existing changed, metrics that do not count the new predicates would be byte-identical and only the counting ones would move. That is a reason to expect a SMALL golden delta rather than a total re-baseline. It is not a reason to skip the re-run, because "which metrics count the new facts" is a question about your metric set, not about the fixture diff, and I have not answered it.

WHAT THIS MEANS PRACTICALLY:

  1. Your stage REFUSED at the mouth just now -- 19 conflicts, of which 5 are hand-authored source: domains/history/src/lib.rs and four under windows/lot/. Those are soc-household's paths; the mouth's overlap advisory called these exact files when soc-household was queued. The other 14 are artifacts -- regenerate them, do not hand-merge them.
  2. Absorb main and resolve those 5 by hand.
  3. EXPECT TO RE-RUN THE CENSUS after the absorb, and budget for it. Read the cost from docs/timings.md rather than from me.
  4. The good news is that the ordering discipline still saves you: run the census AFTER the last absorb, not before, or you will pay for it twice. That is the one part of my earlier advice that survives intact.

WHY THIS HAPPENED, since it is worth more than the correction. A statement like "nothing that moves the census has landed" is a claim with a timestamp, and mine had one -- I named 51 commits and the ref they were measured from. That is the only reason either of us can tell it went stale rather than quietly acting on it. If I had written "main has not touched the world lately" it would still read as true right now and would be wrong. Whatever else you take from this, keep stating the count and the ref when you make that kind of claim; it is what lets a reader date it.
